## Overview `has_xgrammar_unsupported_json_features` treats every `integer` + `multipleOf` schema as unsupported, so these schemas fall back to guidance under `auto` and are rejected when the backend is `xgrammar`. The pinned xgrammar (0.2.8) does enforce `multipleOf` for integers, but only within limits: the value must be an integer in [1, 1024] and the schema must have no `minimum`/`maximum` bound. Outside those limits it logs a warning and ignores the constraint, as it always does for `number`. This PR lets the enforced subset use xgrammar and keeps gating everything else. @errmakov pointed out that integer `multipleOf` is enforced in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48416#issuecomment-5732951369 (thanks!). Tracker: #12131. ## Claims - `{"type": "integer", "multipleOf": N}` with an integer `N` in [1, 1024] and no bounds (also nested in objects and in type lists like `["integer", "null"]`) now uses xgrammar, and the grammar enforces it. For `multipleOf: 5`, `10` and `-15` are accepted and `7` is rejected. - Everything xgrammar 0.2.8 would silently ignore stays gated, so it still falls back to guidance as on main: `number` + `multipleOf`, non-integer `multipleOf` (`2.5`), `multipleOf > 1024`, and integer `multipleOf` with any of `minimum`/`maximum`/`exclusiveMinimum`/`exclusiveMaximum`. ## Validation ```bash pytest tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_xgrammar.py tests/v1/structured_output/test_validation.py -k "multipleOf or multiple_of or falls_back" pytest tests/v1/structured_output/ tests/parser/ ``` ```text # main (new tests, old gate) FAILED test_backend_xgrammar.py::TestHasXGrammarUnsupportedJsonFeatures::test_supported_json_features[supported_integer_multipleOf_schemas] AssertionError: Schema should be supported: {'type': 'integer', 'multipleOf': 120} 1 failed, 7 passed # this PR 8 passed ``` On CPU with xgrammar 0.2.8: - `tests/v1/structured_output/`: 275 passed, 2 xfailed with this PR (272 passed on main). The same 2 tests fail on main and with this PR (`TestPR58067Regressions::test_disable_any_whitespace_is_{false,true}`, a fixture-discovery error unrelated to this change). - `tests/parser/` (without `tests/parser/cohere`, which needs an optional package): 6791 passed on main and with this PR. - `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `pre-commit run --files` pass on the changed files. End to end on CPU through vLLM's path (`_validate_structured_outputs` with `backend="auto"`, then `XgrammarBackend.compile_grammar` and `accept_tokens`, gpt2 tokenizer): - `{"score": {"type": "integer", "multipleOf": 5}}`: `auto` picks xgrammar. `{"score": 10}` and `{"score": -15}` are accepted and `{"score": 7}` is rejected. - The same schema with `"minimum": 0`: `auto` still picks guidance.
What xgrammar 0.2.8 enforces for integer multipleOf (checked with Grammar.from_json_schema) | schema | accepts a non-multiple? | |---|---| | `multipleOf: 5` | no (enforced) | | `multipleOf: 2.0` | no (enforced) | | `multipleOf: 1024` | no (enforced) | | `multipleOf: 2.5` | yes (ignored, warning) | | `multipleOf: 1025` | yes (ignored, warning) | | `multipleOf: 7, minimum: 0` (or `maximum`, `exclusiveMinimum`, `exclusiveMaximum` alone) | yes (ignored, warning) | | `multipleOf: 7, minimum: 0, maximum: 10000` | yes (ignored, warning) | | `multipleOf: 7, minimum: 0, maximum: 20` | no (enforced) | The last row (both bounds and a narrow range) is enforced, but this PR keeps all bounded cases gated to stay conservative; it can be widened later.
## Details - `_xgrammar_enforces_integer_multiple_of` returns whether `multipleOf` is an integer value in [1, 1024] (rejecting `bool`) with no bound keys. The gate returns unsupported for `number` + `multipleOf`, or for `integer` + `multipleOf` when that helper is false. - Tests: integer cases move from the unsupported fixture to a new supported one, and the out-of-limit cases are added to the unsupported fixture. `test_integer_multiple_of_is_enforced` / `test_integer_multiple_of_is_ignored_outside_limits` check the xgrammar behavior the gate relies on, next to the existing grammar-acceptance tests. - `test_abstract_parser.py` used `integer` + `multipleOf: 2` as its xgrammar-unsupported example; it now uses `number` + `multipleOf: 0.5`, like the test next to it. `test_validation.py`'s fallback case gains `"minimum": 0` so it still falls back. - #62877 also edits the `test_validation.py` parametrize touched here; whichever lands second needs a small rebase. AI assistance: Claude Code was used to draft the change, the tests and this description. I reviewed the changes and the test results before submitting. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

files.patch:
@@ -36,8 +36,24 @@ def unsupported_multipleOf_schemas():
     return [
         {"type": "number", "multipleOf": 120},
         {"Even": {"type": "number", "multipleOf": 2}},
+        {"type": ["integer", "number"], "multipleOf": 2},
+        # integer + multipleOf outside the limits xgrammar enforces
+        {"type": "integer", "multipleOf": 2.5},
+        {"type": "integer", "multipleOf": 1025},
+        {"type": "integer", "multipleOf": 7, "minimum": 0},
+        {"type": "integer", "multipleOf": 7, "exclusiveMaximum": 100},
+        {"type": "integer", "multipleOf": 7, "minimum": 0, "maximum": 20},
+    ]
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def supported_integer_multipleOf_schemas():
+    return [
         {"type": "integer", "multipleOf": 120},
+        {"type": "integer", "multipleOf": 1024},
+        {"type": "integer", "multipleOf": 2.0},
         {"Even": {"type": "integer", "multipleOf": 2}},
+        {"type": ["integer", "null"], "multipleOf": 3},
     ]
 
 
@@ -397,6 +413,7 @@ def test_unsupported_json_features(self, schema_type, request):
         "schema_type",
         [
             "supported_frankenstein_schema",
+            "supported_integer_multipleOf_schemas",
             "pattern_properties_schema",
             "property_names_schema",
             "property_names_with_additional_properties_schema",
@@ -460,6 +477,18 @@ def test_supported_list_type_json_features(self, schema):
 
 
 class TestIsGrammarAcceptString:
+    def test_integer_multiple_of_is_enforced(self):
+        schema = {"type": "integer", "multipleOf": 5}
+        assert grammar_accepts(schema, "10")
+        assert grammar_accepts(schema, "-15")
+        assert not grammar_accepts(schema, "7")
+
+    def test_integer_multiple_of_is_ignored_outside_limits(self):
+        # These must stay gated in has_xgrammar_unsupported_json_features
+        assert grammar_accepts({"type": "integer", "multipleOf": 2.5}, "7")
+        assert grammar_accepts({"type": "integer", "multipleOf": 1025}, "5")
+        assert grammar_accepts({"type": "integer", "multipleOf": 7, "minimum": 0}, "8")
+
     class TestPR42904Support:
         def test_property_names_constrains_keys(self, property_names_schema):
             assert grammar_accepts(property_names_schema, '{"score": 5}')

@@ -313,11 +313,11 @@ def test_unhandled_spec_is_a_validation_error(validate):
 @pytest.mark.parametrize(
     "schema, expected_backend",
     [
-        # multipleOf is unsupported by xgrammar.
+        # multipleOf is unsupported by xgrammar for number and for bounded integer.
         (
             {
                 "type": "object",
-                "properties": {"n": {"type": "integer", "multipleOf": 2}},
+                "properties": {"n": {"type": "integer", "multipleOf": 2, "minimum": 0}},
             },
             "guidance",
         ),

@@ -347,6 +347,22 @@ def _has_pattern_and_length_bounds(schema: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
     )
 
 
+def _xgrammar_enforces_integer_multiple_of(schema: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
+    """Return whether xgrammar (pinned 0.2.8) enforces integer multipleOf.
+
+    It only does so for integer values in [1, 1024] without any
+    minimum/maximum bound; otherwise it ignores multipleOf with a warning."""
+    multiple_of = schema.get("multipleOf")
+    if isinstance(multiple_of, bool) or not isinstance(multiple_of, int | float):
+        return False
+    if not (1 <= multiple_of <= 1024 and float(multiple_of).is_integer()):
+        return False
+    return not any(
+        key in schema
+        for key in ("minimum", "maximum", "exclusiveMinimum", "exclusiveMaximum")
+    )
+
+
 # FIXME(arpera): The approach used here needs to be redesigned because of
 # existing bugs: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57550
 def _schema_types(schema: dict[str, Any]) -> set[str]:
@@ -368,14 +384,21 @@ def check_object(obj: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
 
         schema_types = _schema_types(obj)
 
-        # integer/number + multipleOf is unsupported by xgrammar
+        # number + multipleOf is unsupported by xgrammar
         # This is known behavior and xgrammar emits warning in logs:
-        #   [21:18:08] /project/cpp/json_schema_converter.cc:1053:
         #   Warning: multipleOf is not supported for type:number; ignoring multipleOf
         # This warning was added in PR
         # https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar/pull/670
         # So, no need to track progress on this
-        if (schema_types & {"integer", "number"}) and ("multipleOf" in obj):
+        # integer + multipleOf is only enforced within the limits checked in
+        # _xgrammar_enforces_integer_multiple_of; otherwise it is ignored too
+        if "multipleOf" in obj and (
+            "number" in schema_types
+            or (
+                "integer" in schema_types
+                and not _xgrammar_enforces_integer_multiple_of(obj)
+            )
+        ):
             return True
 
         # array + some constraints is unsupported by xgrammar
